subject: Recap & next steps: integration architecture, SDK/auth, and prompt governance
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finoptics.com>; Priya Rao <priya@finoptics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: integration architecture, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope before the workshop: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Primary use case: multi-tenant customer support assistant (ticket triage + suggested responses + internal tool triggers).
- Traffic profile: ~150 req/s peak, median 40 req/s. Typical request: short prompt (20–80 tokens) then streaming response with tool calls.
- Data residency / compliance: FinOptics prefers data processed in a VPC / AW S region (us-west-2) and has GDPR considerations for embeddings storage.

Technical items / questions we promised to follow up on:
1) SDK setup & auth model
   - Options discussed: Redwood Hosted API vs Redwood Private (VPC). You indicated preference for Private or Private-like connectivity (PrivateLink).
   - Action: provide SDK onboarding steps and recommended auth pattern (API token + KMS-backed rotation or mTLS). See attached sdk-auth-guide.md.

2) Routing & deployment policy
   - We recommended a canary-first route (smaller model variant for 10% traffic) with automated fallback to stable variant. Need to validate SLA impact.

3) Structured output / tool calling
   - Plan: use function-calling for structured JSON outputs (schema validation on both sides). We'll suggest strict JSON schema enforcement to avoid prompt injection into tool arguments.

4) Embeddings & reranker strategy
   - Suggest hybrid approach: sparse retrieval + dense ANN (FAISS/Weaviate) with a cross-encoder re-ranker for top-k. We'll outline storage options that avoid sending full PII to third-party indexes.

5) Prompt templates & governance
   - Propose a simple versioning policy (prompt-template v{major}.{minor}) stored in Git, with an approvals checklist and automated evals for regression detection. See attached prompt-governance.md for a starter template.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- FinOptics: share the technical contact for the deep integration workshop (networking, security) 
- Redwood: schedule 90-minute integration workshop (we propose Mar 2 or Mar 4, 10am PT). Camila will lead the integration walkthrough; Vivek will scope VPC connectivity and auth.
- Post-workshop: Redwood to produce an integration checklist + draft SOW (we'll include SLA and onboarding milestones).

Attachments: integration-checklist.xlsx, sdk-auth-guide.md

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finoptics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finoptics.com>, FinOptics Tech <tech@finoptics.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: integration architecture, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Thanks Neha — this is great, thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Connectivity: we are on AWS (us-west-2). We prefer PrivateLink or VPC peering to avoid public egress for model requests. Can you confirm Redwood Private supports PrivateLink or a VPC connector?

- Auth: our security team prefers token-based auth backed by KMS and optionally mTLS for service-to-service. We want key rotation and audit logs tied to KMS. Does Redwood support KMS integration for keys and audit logging?

- Embeddings: we cannot host customer PII in third-party SaaS vector stores. We need options: host embeddings in our VPC (managed by us) or Redwood to host with an agreement that PII is never stored. Also need retention controls and deletions (we will need proof for GDPR).

- Prompt safety: are there any built-in guards for prompt-injection (e.g., input sanitization, forcing the model to adhere to system prompt, user input escaping) you recommend out-of-the-box? We want to see a short design doc or controls list.

We can do Mar 2 at 10am PT for the integration workshop. I'll bring our infra lead (Priya) and a secops engineer.

On attachments: can you send the SDK onboarding steps as a short checklist (we saw sdk-auth-guide.md but would appreciate a one-page checklist we can hand to our infra team)?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Product, FinOptics
alex.kim@finoptics.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finoptics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: integration architecture, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Alex — appreciate the clarity. Quick technical note ahead of the workshop so we can focus on the items you flagged: 

1) Connectivity options
- Redwood Private supports VPC peering and PrivateLink in us-west-2. For strict network isolation we’ll run the control plane as a thin managed plane and the data plane (model-serving) inside your VPC via our Private agent. Vivek, can we bring the VPC connector docs to the workshop?

2) Auth & KMS
- Recommended pattern: short-lived tokens issued from your KMS (via a small token broker in your VPC) plus mutual TLS for service-to-service calls. This gives you rotation and auditable KMS-backed keys. Redwood logs and ties request IDs to tokens for audit trails. See sdk-auth-guide.md attachment for step-by-step.

3) Embeddings storage & GDPR
- Two viable paths:
  a) Host embeddings in FinOptics-managed ANN store in your VPC (preferred for PII).
  b) Redwood hosts embeddings under a specific contract with retention & deletion policies; we can provide export + purge endpoints and SOC2 attestations.

4) Retrieval + reranking architecture
- Suggest hybrid retrieval: BM25 (Elastic) for recall followed by Faiss/Weaviate ANN, then a lightweight cross-encoder on Redwood for top-32 re-rank. This keeps expensive cross-encoder calls small and local.

5) Structured output / tool calling
- Use function-calling with strict JSON schema and server-side validation to avoid prompt-injected tool args. We can also canonicalize user text before passing to the model.

6) Prompt governance & injection mitigations
- Controls to implement pre-launch:
  * Prompt template versioning (vA.B) stored in Git with PR reviews and CI checks.
  * Automated regression/eval suite that runs key prompts on every PR (score drift alerts).
  * Input sanitization layers and allowlisting/denylisting for tool arguments.
  * Runtime flags to lock system prompts (read-only in prod) and a staging environment for template changes.
  * Red-team cadence: quarterly adversarial tests + targeted injection tests before major releases.

I attached a starter prompt-governance.md with suggested policies and a short CLI to tag prompt versions. Vivek — I asked the infra team to prepare the VPC connector diagram and a short checklist for KMS integration for the workshop.

Marissa — loop in legal for the hosting/retention options and SOW language.

Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
